title: University of Baltistan, Skardu
content:
Introduction
The Department of Tourism and Hospitality Management at the University of Baltistan, Skardu, established in November 2018, aims to address the growing need for educated and well-trained tourism professionals in Gilgit-Baltistan. This region, representing Pakistan’s premier attraction for international and national tourists, is home to some of the world’s highest peaks, including the second-highest, K2. The vast glaciers, valleys, rivers, lakes, orchards, and rich cultural heritage of Gilgit-Baltistan offer huge potential to develop tourism as a robust industry. Our department is strategically positioned to create a tourism-friendly business environment in this region, located at the intersection of four great mountain ranges: the Himalayas, Karakoram, Hindukush, and Pamir. It lies along the historic Silk Route, now transformed into the China Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), further enhancing its significance. We aim to develop a cadre of tourism professionals equipped with the necessary skills to manage and promote tourism effectively. Our curriculum combines theoretical knowledge with practical experience, preparing students for careers in tourism and hospitality management. We currently offer a 2-year Associate Degree and a 4-year BS in Tourism and Hospitality Management, with plans to expand our programs to include comprehensive undergraduate options like Culinary Arts Management, as well as postgraduate studies. Collaborations with local and international organizations, such as the Gilgit-Baltistan Tourism Department, PTDC, the Hotel Association, the Tour Operator Association, the Photography Association of Gilgit-Baltistan, UNWTO, and WTTC, will provide opportunities for hands-on training and job placements.

Our commitment extends to enhancing the local economy, preserving natural and cultural heritage, and contributing to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) through innovative and sustainable tourism practices.

content:
Introduction
The Department of Educational Development is one of the pioneering academic units of the University of Baltistan, Skardu, Pakistan. It is dedicated to promoting excellence in teacher education, educational research, and professional development within the regional and national context. The department aims to produce competent teachers, teacher educators, educational managers, and leaders equipped with relevant knowledge, pedagogical skills, ethical values, and a strong foundation in research and scholarship. The department currently offers BS Education, B.Ed. Education, and MPhil in Education programs in line with the guidelines of the Higher Education Commission (HEC) of Pakistan. These programs are designed to integrate theory with practice, fostering critical thinking, reflective practice, and innovation among students. Through its academic and research initiatives, the department contributes to improving the quality of education and addressing contemporary educational challenges at both regional and national levels.

title: University of Baltistan, Skardu
content:
Event Overview
A dignified and grand ceremony was held at the University of Baltistan, Skardu, in connection with Pakistan Day, March 23. Faculty members and students participated enthusiastically. The purpose of the event was to pay tribute to the martyrs of the Pakistan Movement and to highlight the importance of the Ideology of Pakistan. The ceremony formally began with prayers for the prosperity and dignity of the motherland, followed by a flag-hoisting ceremony. The university premises echoed with slogans of “Pakistan Zindabad.” On this occasion, the national anthem was sung and special prayers were offered for the country’s security and stability. Vice Chancellor Professor Dr. Masood Akhtar, in his message, encouraged the youth to strengthen Pakistan through education, innovation, and integrity. He stated that the youth are the true strength of the nation and the driving force that can lead the country forward through knowledge, creativity, and honesty. He expressed his commitment to building a prosperous and modern Pakistan where every citizen has the opportunity to progress. University faculty members Dr. Zakir Hussain Zakir, Dr. Haji Karim Khan, and Nasir Abbas also addressed the gathering. The speakers expressed that March 23 is a historic day when the Muslims of the subcontinent determined their destiny and laid the foundation of the Two-Nation Theory. It was this very ideology that made the establishment of a free Islamic state on the world map possible. The speakers warned that hostile forces are seeking to undermine Pakistan, the stronghold of Islam, but emphasized that the Pakistani nation stands united. Every citizen, they said, is like a solid wall, ready to make any sacrifice for the country’s stability. They stressed that to confront current challenges, the nation must revive the same spirit that prevailed at the time of Pakistan’s creation. They pledged that together they would work for the honor and elevation of the green crescent flag. By following the principles set forth by Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah and striving to fulfill the dream of Allama Iqbal, the country would be steered toward progress and prosperity. At the conclusion of the ceremony, sweets were distributed among the students, and a renewed commitment was made that through dedication and hard work in the field of education, Pakistan can be made a great nation. title: University of Baltistan, Skardu
content:
Event Overview
The University of Baltistan, Skardu organized a comprehensive awareness rally to promote awareness against drug abuse and encourage a drug-free campus environment. The rally was attended by a large number of students, faculty members, administrative officers, and university staff. Officials from the Anti-Narcotics Force (ANF), who specially visited from Gilgit, also participated in the event. The rally was led by the Registrar, Dr. Mir Alam, and the Focal Person of the Drug-Free Campus Committee, Dr. Shafqat Hussain. Participants carried placards and banners displaying messages highlighting the harmful effects of drugs and emphasizing the need to protect the younger generation from this social menace. Addressing the participants, Dr. Shafqat Hussain stated that maintaining a drug-free University of Baltistan is a shared responsibility of all stakeholders. He emphasized that a healthy, progressive, and prosperous society cannot be achieved unless this menace is eliminated from society. He further stated that youth are a valuable asset and raising awareness among them about the harmful effects of drugs is the need of the hour. He added that the University of Baltistan will continue organizing awareness programs, seminars, and walks to eliminate drug abuse and promote awareness among students in order to create a safe and positive educational environment. Registrar Dr. Mir Alam thanked the Anti-Narcotics Force officials for their special participation from Gilgit and appreciated their efforts in combating drug abuse. He stated that only through collaboration between educational institutions and law enforcement agencies can the younger generation be protected from social evils such as drug addiction. At the conclusion of the rally, participants reaffirmed their commitment to actively contribute to the ongoing anti-drug campaign and fulfill their responsibilities toward establishing a drug-free society. Furthermore, students of the Department of Chemistry played a key role in organizing and managing the awareness program. They actively contributed to planning the rally, guiding participants, preparing banners and placards, and supporting various administrative arrangements. The university administration appreciated the efforts of the Chemistry students and emphasized that active youth participation is essential to making this campaign against drugs successful.

title: University of Baltistan, Skardu
content:
Event Overview
The University of Baltistan, Skardu, celebrated Kashmir Solidarity Day with traditional enthusiasm and patriotic fervor. The day began with an inspiring speech competition held in the Senate Hall, where female students captivated the audience with their passionate addresses on the right to self-determination for the Kashmiri people. Addressing the event, Vice Chancellor Professor Dr. Masood Akhtar stated that the Kashmir issue is not merely a regional conflict but a matter of humanity, whose solution lies in the aspirations of the Kashmiri people and the resolutions of the United Nations. He lauded the extraordinary resilience of the Kashmiri people and called upon the international community to end the ongoing violations of human rights. Other speakers included Dean of Social Sciences Professor Ashfaq Ahmad Shah , who emphasized that the gathering was to show solidarity with the Kashmiri brothers and convey to the world that Pakistan stands with them. Deputy Director Student Affairs Nasir Abbas highlighted the purpose of the event, stating that the University of Baltistan continuously strives to promote national ideals. He added that Kashmir Day is observed to showcase the atrocities in Indian-occupied Kashmir and to affirm that Pakistan stands with the Kashmiri people in their struggle against oppression. Associate Professor Botany Dr. Ishtiaq Hussain Mondoq, the focal person expressed gratitude and appreciated the organizers for their tireless efforts, while Assistant Professor Dr. Muhammad Riaz supervised the speech competition. The results of the competition were as follows: First Position: Syeda Nosheen Zahra (Department of Educational Development) Second Position: Aliza (Department of Linguistics and Literature) Third Position: Ambreen Fatima (Department of Linguistics and Literature) Special honors included recitation by Lecturer Muhammad Kamal and the Naat of the Prophet ﷺ presented by Director IT, Imtiaz Ahmed. The event was expertly moderated by student Razia Hameed. The judges for the competition were Dr. Muhammad Hassan, Dr. Muhammad Nazir, and Dr. Zulfiqar Ali. In addition to the speeches, a short rally was organized from the main gate to the Admin Block. A large number of faculty, administrative officers, and students participated, holding banners and pamphlets condemning Indian atrocities in occupied Kashmir. The demonstrators stated that India’s oppressive actions have now been exposed to the world, and the international community recognizes India’s suppression of Kashmiri freedom. They affirmed that the Kashmiri people cannot be kept under force for long, as every child in the region is now awakened to fight for their freedom. It is worth noting that the administration, faculty, and students of the University of Baltistan consistently observe national events with zeal and reaffirm their unwavering commitment to recognizing the inalienable right to self-determination of the Kashmiri people . title: University of Baltistan, Skardu
content:
Event Overview
The Capacity Building Training Program commenced with an inaugural session led by resource person Mr. Umar Saeed Qadri, focusing on institutional strengthening, leadership, professional development, and sustainable higher education, with Vice Chancellor Prof. Dr. Masood Akhtar emphasized that the training had been organized to conduct a comprehensive review of the administrative and academic systems of the university. The second day featured interactive sessions on people management in the contemporary era, professional etiquette, ethics, diversity, equity, and inclusion, equipping academic, administrative, and finance officials with practical leadership and management skills to enhance institutional performance and governance. The three-day Capacity Building Training Program for Principal Officers and Senior Management Team concluded at the University of Baltistan, Skardu, with a closing ceremony attended by university leadership, participants, and officials. On the final day, resource person Mr. Umar Saeed Kadri delivered sessions on Leadership in the VUCA Era & Industry 5.0, SDGs 2030: World vs. Pakistan, Progress & Roadmap, Modern Leadership and Management Practices from the Islamic Perspective, and an Integration Workshop that linked public financial management, ethics, leadership, and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) to practical institutional scenarios. During the closing ceremony, Director Professional & Skill Development, Dr. Haji Karim Khan, welcomed the participants and presented a briefing on the training program. In his address, Vice Chancellor Prof. Dr. Masood Akhtar appreciated the valuable contributions of the resource person, Mr. Umar Saeed Kadri, and Dr. Haji Karim Khan for successfully organizing the training program. He emphasized that individuals should always remain prepared to face emerging challenges and changing circumstances. He noted that reading books broadens knowledge and enhances problem-solving abilities. He further stated that a true leader leads by example, believing in hard work and inspiring others through personal commitment. Highlighting the importance of practical competence, he remarked that "a degree is merely a piece of paper; it is the combination of education and professional skills that truly makes an individual successful." The Vice Chancellor further emphasized that such capacity-building initiatives are essential for strengthening the professional competencies of employees and enhancing institutional performance. He highlighted the importance of continuous professional development in higher education institutions, stating that regular training equips human resources with the knowledge and skills required to meet evolving workplace demands and global standards. He urged participants to embrace lifelong learning and continuously update themselves according to the needs of the time. Speaking on behalf of the participants, Dr. Zakir Hussain Zakir, Director Planning & Development (P&D), expressed gratitude to the university administration and the resource person for organizing a highly informative and practical training program that would contribute to improving institutional effectiveness. Certificates were distributed among the participants, while souvenir and gifts were presented to Mr. Umar Saeed Kadri in recognition of his outstanding services as the lead trainer. The ceremony concluded with a vote of thanks by Dr. Haji Karim Khan, while Mr. Abdul Rehman Mir, Lecturer, served as the master of ceremony.

Event Overview
The Department of Zoology, University of Baltistan Skardu, in collaboration with Ev-K2-CNR and UNDP, organized a one-day webinar on “Major Parasitic Zoonosis and Diagnostic Techniques of Domestic and Wild Animals of Gilgit-Baltistan” under the Water for Development (W4D) project funded by the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS). The session was chaired by Prof. Dr. Masood Akhtar, Vice Chancellor, University of Baltistan. The Vice Chancellor appreciated Ev-K2-CNR’s support in establishing a dedicated zoonotic laboratory at the university through the provision of modern laboratory equipment, noting that the facility would strengthen practical research and scientific problem-solving in the region. Concluding the two-day webinar series, which also included “Advanced Phytosanitary Training on Major Stone Fruits of Gilgit-Baltistan”, Prof. Dr. Akhtar acknowledged Ev-K2-CNR, UNDP, and AICS for their support and emphasized that such research-driven initiatives would advance animal and plant disease research in Gilgit-Baltistan. International experts led the technical sessions. Prof. Dr. Luca Rossi provided training on the detection of endo- and ecto-zoonotic parasites, while Ms. Liliana addressed wildlife and livestock diseases, control measures, and the growing risk of zoonotic transmission. Dr. Shahid Ali, Head of the Department of Zoology, highlighted the webinar’s role in fostering research collaboration and knowledge sharing on parasitic diseases affecting animals and humans in the region. Dr. Muhammad Ali noted that the project had strengthened diagnostic and research capacity by equipping students and researchers with advanced skills and techniques. Project updates were presented by Mr. Riaz ul Hassan and Mr. Aurangzaib, representatives of Ev-K2-CNR, while Dr. Ishtiaq Hussain, Head of the Department of Botany and Focal Person of the project, stressed the importance of sustained capacity-building to enhance diagnostic capabilities in Zoology and Botany and to safeguard the ecosystems of Gilgit-Baltistan.

title: University of Baltistan, Skardu
content:
Event Overview
Yak is a Unique Treasure for the Region’s Economy, Say the Vice Chancellor and Other Experts Skardu (April 13, 2026): A one-day national symposium and workshop titled “Yak: A Unique Treasure of the Region” was jointly organized by the University of Baltistan, Skardu, and the Virtual University of Pakistan, Islamabad. A large number of national and international researchers participated in the workshop. The event was chaired by the Vice Chancellor of the University of Baltistan, Professor Dr. Masood Akhtar, who attended as the chief guest. In his address, he elaborated in detail—drawing on his expertise as a zoologist—on the importance, utility, and existing challenges related to yak research and development. This symposium, which has been organized consistently over the past four years, featured a visiting professor from Brazil who presented a paper on the anatomy of the yak. Other experts shared the latest scientific insights on yak genetics and diseases affecting the species. Dr. Ali Hamza participated online via video link and shared his experiences regarding entrepreneurship opportunities. The workshop was attended by the Deans and Directors of the University of Baltistan, along with MPhil and PhD scholars from the Department of Zoology. A significant number of teachers and students from Government Boys Degree College, Government Degree College for Women, and Public School and College were also present. Experts informed participants about contemporary research on yak in China and other neighboring countries and its impact on the local economy. In addition to the academic sessions, a one-hour essay writing competition was organized for students, in which approximately 22 students participated. Students from Government Degree College for Women secured first and second positions, while the third position was awarded to the University of Baltistan. The focal persons of the workshop, Associate Professor and Director Academics Dr. Ghulam Raza from the University of Baltistan and Dr. Tanveer from the Virtual University of Pakistan, spoke in detail about the organization, objectives, and significance of the program. The primary aim of the workshop was to raise awareness among the local community and farmers about improved yak breeding practices, modern management techniques, and the economic benefits associated with yak farming. In the second phase of the symposium, a “Farmer Field Day” will be held in Shigar, where a practical demonstration of yak will be arranged to benefit communities in areas where yak populations are limited. In conclusion, Vice Chancellor Professor Dr. Masood Akhtar appreciated the efforts of the entire team and termed the event a milestone for the sustainable development of the region.

title: University of Baltistan, Skardu
content:
Event Overview
Skardu, June 17, 2026: The Department of Botany, in collaboration with the Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences, University of Baltistan (UoB), observed the International Day to Combat Desertification and Drought through a series of awareness and educational activities aimed at promoting sustainable land management and environmental conservation. The event commenced with a welcome address by Dr. Ishtiaq Hussain, Head of the Department of Botany, who highlighted the significance of the day and emphasized the need for collective efforts to address the challenges of desertification and drought. Prof. Dr. Masood Akhtar, Vice Chancellor, University of Baltistan, addressed the participants and underscored the importance of combating land degradation through awareness, research, and community engagement. He emphasized the role of academic institutions in developing sustainable solutions to environmental challenges keeping indigenous practices and SDGs and to support national economy through Agriculture and Livestock initiatives. A symbolic awareness walk was organized from the Administration Block to Academic Block-II, involving faculty members, students, and university staff, demonstrating their commitment to environmental stewardship. The technical session featured presentations by Experts of forest Department, Central Karakoram National Park (CKNP) and Deosai National Park (DNP), delivered a presentation on land degradation and forest conservation, on biodiversity conservation and sustainable natural resource management in protected areas. Both Focal Persons Dr. Muhammad Qasim and Dr. Muhammad Akbar Zaigham, Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences and Botany shared their views in the concluding remarks appreciated the active participation of students and faculty and stressed the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration for environmental sustainability and acknowledged the contributions of the Vice Chancellor, guest speakers, faculty members, students, organizing team, and participants for making the event successful. The proceedings were efficiently conducted by Ms. Sajida Batool, (Master of Ceremony) of the program. Faculty members, students, and staff from both departments actively participated in the event, reaffirming their commitment to environmental protection, sustainable land-use practices, and collective action against desertification and drought.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
UNIVERSITY OF BALTISTAN, SKARDU
University of Baltistan, Skardu (UoBS) shall make admissions to its degree programs,
Diplomas, and Certificate Courses duly approved by the relevant bodies by adopting a
procedure prescribed in the admission policy and the university calendar. A new program shall
be initiated by the Head of the (relevant) Department and is duly approved by the Dean of the
Faculty, the Univ ersity Admission Committee (UAC), the Academic Council, and the
Syndicate.
At present, UoBS is offering admissions to the following programs in the teaching departments.
A. Bachelor Studies (BS) 4 Years

A copy of the printed Admission Policy UoBS 2021 shall be made available in all the
departments and affiliated colleges as well as the university library and on the website for the
information and guidance of the students, parents, and the public at large.
Admission Regulations in General
The following shall be the rules and regulations of admissions for all the Degree Programs,
Diplomas, and Certificate Courses.
1. Admissions shall be made strictly on merit (including the reserved seats, however,
their merit will be determined separately) in accordance with the criteria laid down by
the University Admission Committee (UAC) from time to time.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
2. The UAC shall announce the Admissions Campaign each year in September/October
and shall close the admission campaign by the following November before winter
vacations.
3. Merit shall be determined based on the required terminal degree.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
4. The 3rd division in the terminal degree shall not be acceptable for admission to UoBS
in any Degree Program.
5. The University Admission Committee (UAC) shall have the power to decide on issues
and hardship cases according to the Admission Policy UoBS. However, the committee
shall be bound to seek the anticipatory approval of the Vice-Chancellor and the
Academic Council in all such cases.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
6. The UAC shall have the power to revise the admission criteria, before launching the
admission campaign, however, with the anticipatory approval of the Vice-Chancellor
and the Academic Council.
7. For all the programs class size shall not be less than 10; however, for Ph.D. Programs
shall not be less than five (05). However, under special circumstances, the minimum
class size may be reduced to five (05) with special permission from the competent
authority

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
8. Any student, who had previously been rusticated, expelled, or whose entry in an y of
the Departments/Colleges/Institutes/Centres was banned for any reason whatsoever at
any time during his/her academic career, or any person declared persona non-grata
shall not be admitted to any program or class (one session) without the permission of
the Vice-Chancellor on the recommendations of the Chairperson, followed by the
Director Student Affairs (DSA) and the concerned Dean office. The Office of the DSA
will circulate a complete list of such students to all the Departments, against whom
any kind of disciplinary action has been taken. The case of admission/re-admission of
all such students will be processed in light of the university regulations.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
9. All difficulties connected with the admissions shall be resolved by the UAC in
consultation with the Chairperson/Principal/Head of the Department; and shall deem
to be settled with the approval of the Vice-Chancellor later.
10. Any Reserved Seat which remains unfilled at the closing date (or extended period),
shall not be transferred to the Merit Seats.
[Page 5]
Page 4 of 15

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
11. Age limit
i. A candidate for the BS Program shall not be older than 26 years on the last date
fixed for the receipt of the applications for admission. However, in special cases,
as decided by the University Admission Committee (UAC), and if seats are
available, the candidates above 26 years of age can be reconsidered for
admission if he/she meets the merit criteria otherwise.
ii. Age limit shall not be applicable to the following categories of candidates:
 Employee/Spouse seeking admission against the reserved seats
 Pakistani Armed Forces
 Government Teacher seeking admission against the reserved seats
iii. The age limit for government employees / autonomous bodies shall be followed
as per Government rules if they submit the NOC and study leave from the
competent authority to pursue their studies at UoBS. However, the seat shall not
exceed their prescribed quota.
iv. The age limit shall not be applicable to B.Ed., MBA Executive , and
MS/MPhil/Ph.D. Programs.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
12. If two or more candidates fall at the same position on the list of merit, the older one
shall be placed higher on the merit list.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
13. A candidate having a qualification/certificate/degree without English as a
compulsory/elective/optional subject shall not be admitted to any program at UoBS.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
14. If equivalence of any qualification/certificate/degree is required, the case shall be
forwarded with comments from the HoD of the Department to the Chairperson
Admission Committee for final decision before the last merit list is displayed.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
15. The admission of applicants from other universities shall be subject to the production
of the Equivalence Certificate (if required) from the university/Board before
admissions are closed.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
16. A uniform policy, as laid down in the Admission Regulations, to determine the merit
shall be observed in all the Departments/Colleges/Institutes/Centres/Sub-Campuses.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
17. Criteria for admission of Foreign Studen ts shall be determined by the University
Admission Committee (UAC).
18. All the candidates shall be required to show their original documents/ certificates;
however, the office will not retain their original documents. And the candidates are
required to submit the following documents to the Admissions Office of the UoBS for
consideration of the merit list:
 Admission Processing Fee Slip
 Two copies of all the a cademic recor ds (Transcripts , Degrees, Equivalence
Certificates, etc)
 Copy of domicile certificate
 Three passport-size photographs
 Copy of computerized national identity card (CNIC) or form ‘B’
[Page 6]
Page 5 of 15
 An affidavit signed by the candidate and countersigned by their
mother/father/guardian guaranteeing that the applicant shall not violate the
policy, statutes, rules, and regulations of the UoBS; moreover, they shall
respect university discipline and shall abide by all the rules and regulations of
the UoBS issued from time to time.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
19. After having deposited the due amount of fees at Bank, the students shall submit the
receipt of their Fee Deposit Slip (FDS) in the Admission Office so that he/she may be
issued their Roll Number of the Department.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
20. The dues other than those notified by the University shall not be charged by the
Departments from the students/candidates.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
21. The candidate shall have to deposit their fee as notified by the UoBS within the due
date. After hav ing passed the due date of fee submission, the candidate’s right of
admission shall stand canceled. However, if there is no other eligible candidate in the
waiting, and the seat is lying vacant, the candidate shall seek permission from the
UAC and shall su bmit the due amount fee with a fine (prescribed by UAC and
Treasurer Office) after the due date to secure his/her right of admission.
22. Grade Point Average ( GPA) criteria of UoBS shall be applicable for converting
Cumulative Grade Point Averages ( CGPAs) to percentages for those external
candidates who submit their transcripts with CGPAs only and remained unable to
provide the percentage of marks from their previous university/institute.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
23. All admissions made in contravention of this policy and the rules and regulations of
UoBS shall stand null and void.
24. In case a student remains absent from the class for seven (07) days without having
leave approved by the concerned teacher and the HoD, his/her name shall be removed
from the rolls. However, the students shall be eligible for re -enrolment within three
weeks-time from the date of his/her first absence, on the recommendation of the
Chairperson/HoD, the office of the Dean concerned, and the approval of the Chairman
University Admission Committee (UAC). All such applicants must submit the
prescribed fee of the university before applying for re-enrolment.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
25. The candidates desirous of seeking admission to any program at UoBS must have had
their result of pre -requisite degree/certificate officially notified by the respective
body/authority of their university/Board on or before the closing date of the
admissions.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
26. All issues/queries connected with the admissions shal l be resolved by the University
Admission Committee (UAC).

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
27. As per policy UoBS shall not be bound to provide hostel and transport facilities to the
students.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
28. Only the candidates having Qualifications/Degrees/Certificates duly recognized by
UoBS shall be eligible to apply for admission to UoBS.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
29. The UAC shall be authorized to increase or decrease the number of regular seats
according to the student -teacher ratio as prescribed by HEC (and the accreditation
councils) for BS programs, Diplomas, and Certificate Courses; and the availability of
[Page 7]
Page 6 of 15
research supervision slots for MPhil/Ph.D. programs with the consent of relevant HoD
and concern Dean.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
30. The Vice -Chancellor shall be authorized to increase or decrease the number of
reserved seats for BS programs.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
31. A student/graduate/alumnus may be admitted/re-admitted to a second or subsequent-
Degree program at UoBS as per policy.
32. The degree courses of B.Ed. and MBA Executive can be offered in parallel with other
degrees in the same session or same year. Managing the clash in class timings of their
classes shall solely be the reasonability of the student himself/herself.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
33. The migration of students from another HEC-recognized university to UoBS shall be
governed by the Migration Policy of UoBS. The University Admission Committee
(UAC) and an ad-hoc technical committee of the concerned Department, after having
equated the courses and the credits earned previousl y by the candidate, shall decide
on the admission offer to such candidates.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
34. The applicant shall be responsible to provide an Equivalence Certificate for O Level /
A Level / other equivalent Intermediate Certificate or qualification from foreign
institutes, issued by the Inter Board Committee of Chairmen (IBCC). Provisional
Admission may be granted to such students subject to the provision of the Equivalence
Certificate from the IBCC before the conduct of the First Examinations of the degree
program for which admission was granted.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
35. The marks obtained by a candidate in the additional subject shall neither be counted
nor given any weightage on the list of merit for admission.
Inter-departmental/Inter-program Transfer of Admission

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
36. In the event of vacant seats, inter -departmental/inter-program transfer of admission
files and fees shall be permissible, within one week after the admissions closing date,
on the recommendations of the Chairperson/HoD concerned, with the approval of the
Dean of the Facul ty, provided that, all the merit criteria have been met. The
Chairperson University Admission Committee shall finally confirm such admissions.
Such transfers shall further be subject to:
i. A student who succeeded to secure admission may, on a prescribed application
form, request the Chairperson Admission Committee for transfer of his/her
admission file/fee to a program where at least one seat is lying vacant.
ii. A candidate who failed to secure admission may also, on a prescribed
application form, request the Chairperson Admission Committee for transfer of
his/her admission file/fee to a program where at least one seat is lying vacant.
iii. Transfer request shall be initiated by the student/candidate who shall seek
recommendations of the concerned Chairpersons/HoDs a nd the Dean of the
Faculty, on the prescribed application form, which shall finally be confirmed by
the Chairperson Admission Committee.
[Page 8]
Page 7 of 15
iv. The transfer of admission file/fee shall only be valid after the approval of the
Chairperson Admission Committee.
Seat Allocation for BS Programs

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
37. Seat allocation for BS programs is as follows:
i. Every 4 -year Degree Program shall be enrolling 40 students in the order of
merit.
ii. B.Ed. and MBA Executive shall be enrolling 40 students in the order of merit.
iii. 50% of the total seats in each program shall be reserved for the candidates
having a domicile of Gilgit -Baltistan, and the remaining 50% will be filled in
on open merit bases.
iv. Foreign students shall be required to submit their applications through HEC,
Government of Pakistan. There shall be 10 seats for foreign students in each
program. Their merit will be defined separately. In addition to the normal fee,
there shall be a Special Foreign Fee applicable to foreign students.
v. One (01) seat shall be reserved in each BS Program (including Self -
Support/Afternoon/Evening programs, if any) in addition to the seats on merit
as mentioned above, for the following categories
A. Physically Handicapped Person
B. Sports/Creative Talent
C. Hafiz-e-Quran
D. Pakistani Armed Forces
E. Government Teachers
F. Academic Regular Employee (serving/retired)/Spouse/Children
G. Non-Academic Regular Employee (serving/retired)/Spouse/Children
Admission to 5th Semester

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
38. Candidates possessing a 2-year Associate Degree from UoBS shall be eligible to seek
admission to their relevant BS Program at UoBS.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
39. Candidates possessing a 2 -year Associate Degree from any other HEC-recognized
university shall be eligible to se ek admission to their relevant BS Program at UoBS
only after having equated their courses and their credits earned previously with that of
the UoBS in the relevant program.
BS Exit Program
40. The students of 4-year/5-year Bachelor programs (UOBS and Affiliated Colleges) shall
be allowed to opt for an exit, a fter successful completion of the study of the first two
years. Such students shall be awarded a 2-year Associate Degree.
[Page 9]
Page 8 of 15
Eligibility Criteria for BS Programs

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
41. Eligibility for BS or Equivalent Degree Programs:
i. The candidates having HSSC/FA/FSc/Equivalent Qualification with at least 2nd
division shall be eligible for admission to BS at UoBS.
ii. The eligibility criterion for a specific program will be decided by the relevant
department according to the relevance of the subject studied previously and the
HEC/Accreditation Council from time to time.
iii. Entry Test for BS Programs shall be optional . (Decided by the concern ed
department).
Admissions Against Reserved Seats

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
42. The admission of disabled persons shall be processed through the ad -hoc disability
admission committee constituted to determine candidates’ (type and severity of)
disability. The candidate shall be responsible to provide the disability certificate from
the relevant authority. The department shall forward the cases of disabled persons to
the ad -hoc disability admission committee. This ad -hoc committee shall submit the
final list of selected candidates before the display of the third merit list. There shall be
no relaxation in the given deadline.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
43. The admission on a sports/creative talent basis shall be processed through the ad-hoc
sports admission committee constituted to conduct the trials for respective sports. The
sports office shall be responsible to plan for the trials and submit a final list of the
selected candidates before the display of the third merit list. There shall be no relaxation
in the given deadline.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
44. Admission of the Hafiz-e-Quran candidates shall be processed through the ad-hoc Hifz
admission committee of UoBS. The candidate shall be responsible to provide the Hifz-
e-Quran certificate from the relevant authority. The ad-hoc committee shall give an oral
examination to the candidate(s) and shall send his/her recommendations to the
University Admission Committee (UAC).
45. The above ad-hoc committees will be notified by the chairman UAC.
46. For the armed forces reserved se at, the candidate (children of armed force) shall be
responsible to provide the nomination from the relevant office/quarter. Armed forces
include all the government security organizations i.e., Pakistan Army, Police, Rangers,
etc.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
47. Government Teachers seek ing admission on a reserved seat shall provide a No
Objection Certificate (NOC) issued by the Directorate of Education.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
48. Employees of UoBS seeking admission to any degree program are required to provide
a No Objection Certificate (NOC) issued by the Registrar’s Office before the last date
for submission of the admission application.
[Page 10]
Page 9 of 15

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
49. Children/Spouse of UOBS employees seeking admission on a reserved seat have to
provide a nomination letter from Registrar’s Office.
Admission Regulations for MS/MPhil/PhD
50. Every MS/MPhil/Ph.D. Degree Program shall be enrolling the students in the order of
merit according to the available slots for supervision as per HEC guidelines; i. e. One
PhD-approved supervisor (faculty member) can supervise a maximum of 12 research
students of MS/MPhil/Ph.D. with the condition that the Ph.D. supervisee should be up
to five (05), which may be extended to eight (08) in hard cases with the prior
permission.
51. One (01) seat shall be reserved in each MS/MPhil Program (including Self -
Support/Afternoon/Evening programs, if any) in addition to the seats on merit, for the
following categories:
i. Physically Handicapped Person
ii. Academic Regular Employee (serving/retired)/Spouse/Children
iii. Non-Academic Regular Employee (serving/retired)/Spouse/Children

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
52. The Chairperson/Head of the Departments shall, each year, communicate the number
of available supervisory slots for MS/MPhil/Ph.D., prior to the university admission
campaign.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
53. A candidate having relevant 16 years of education shall be considered eligible for
admission to the corresponding MS/MPhil program.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
54. A candidate having relevant 18 years of education shall be considered eligible for
admission to the corresponding Ph.D. program.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
55. Specific eligibility criteria for different programs may be provided by the relevant
Department / Institute / College / Centre.
56. Entry Tests and interviews for admissions to MS/MPhil and Ph.D. programs shall be
mandatory.
Fee Transfer and Refund Policy

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
57. Fee Transfer and Refund for Regular Programs:
i. Fees and Funds (University and departmental dues) of a student shall be
transferable to any other Department of UoBS subject to the approval of the
Chairperson of the University Admission Committee.
ii. All dues shall be refundable in case of cancellation of admission granted due to
mistake, miscalculation, negligence, or omission on the part of UoBS.
iii. Dues shall not be refundable in case of cancellation of admission if the applicant
was found guilty of (i) providing incorrect information, (ii)
[Page 11]
Page 10 of 15
concealing/distorting the facts, (iii) providing fake certificates , and (iv) using
any other unfair means on the part of the applicant.
iv. Any overpayment shall be refundable only after the fulfillment of all procedural
formalities.
v. The amount of security shall be refundable within three years after the
completion of the degree of the student.

title: ADMISSION POLICY 2021
content:
58. Following tuition fee refund policy shall be applicable if a student withdraws his/her
admission:
i. Full (100%) Tuition Fee shall be refundable up to the 7 th day of convening of
classes
ii. Half (50%) Tuition Fee shall be refundable from the 8th – 15th day of convening
of the classes
iii. No Fee (0%) from the 16th day of convening of classes

title: University of Baltistan, Skardu
content:
Introduction
The Department of Botany, approved by the Academic Council in its 7th meeting held in 2023.The founding Head of Department, Dr. Alamdar Hussain, with a clear vision to harness the high botanical potential of the region and to promote excellence in botanical sciences. From its inception, the department has been committed to developing a strong academic and research culture aligned with regional priorities and global standards. The department is well equipped with modern laboratory facilities and has successfully established a Herbarium and a dedicated Plant Pathology Laboratory. This laboratory has been established under EvK2CNR project(W4Development). It is supported by a team of well-qualified and dedicated faculty members who are actively engaged in teaching, mentoring, and innovative research. The department is involved in cutting-edge research and has initiated the MS program in Botany and aims to launch some other programs including short courses and certificates in the near future. Major areas of specialization include Ecology, Plant Physiology, Plant Pathology, Plant Taxonomy, Ethnobotany, Phytochemistry, Molecular Biology and Biodiversity Conservation. In addition to academics and research, the department maintains strong collaborations with national and international organizations and contributes to society through effective linkages with the Agriculture and Forest Department Gilgit Baltistan, PARC, LUMS and other national universitites for sustainable utilization and processing of natural resources and active engagement with local communities. The department regularly organizes trainings, career counseling sessions, scientific conferences, and workshops, fostering capacity building, innovation, and professional development.

Vision & Mission
Our Vision
The Department of Botany envisions a world where the understanding, appreciation, and sustainable utilization of plant life are central to human well-being and environmental health. Through innovative research, education, and outreach, we aim to unravel the complexities of plant biology, promote biodiversity conservation, and contribute solutions to global challenges such as food security, climate change, and ecosystem restoration. Our department strives to cultivate a diverse and inclusive community of scholars, fostering creativity, collaboration, and leadership in botanical science for the betterment of society and the planet.
Our Mission
The mission of the Department of Botany is to conduct cutting-edge research in plant biology, from molecular mechanisms to ecosystem-level interactions, to deepen our understanding of plant life and its importance to the planet. We are committed to providing high-quality education and training to students, equipping them with the knowledge and skills to address current and future challenges in botany and related fields. Through active engagement with the community, we aim to promote awareness of plant diversity, conservation, and sustainable use, fostering a culture of environmental stewardship and scientific inquiry for the betterment of society and the natural world.

Introduction
The Department of Biological Science
was announced by the then Vice Chancellor Dr. M. Asif Khan during the
visit of President of Pakistan his Excellency Mr. Mamnoon Hussain in
august 2016 on the high demand of public for higher education in Science
subjects. The Department was then approved in 4th academic council hold
on 26th October, 2016. The Department has established its teaching and
research laboratory at first floor of the existing building. The first
batch admissions were offered by the Department in spring 2018 in i.e. BS Botany BS Zoology The
BS programs in Biological Science is to produce competent professionals
acquainted with the latest knowledge about the major disciplines of
Plants and Animal sciences and their challenges in this changing world. This will enable the students to understand the principles of
organizations and inter-relationships in the biological systems with
particular reference to plant and animal diversity. The foundation
courses in Botany includes, Biodiversity and Conservation, Plant
Anatomy, Genetics, Biochemistry, Biostatistics, and the major courses as
Physiology, Genetics, Ecology, Ethnobotany and Cell Biology. The
Zoology as a subject is multidisciplinary in nature, involving study of
organisms and their genetic, morphological and physiological attributes,
their surrounding environment, and their role in conservation of
environment. The animal science is a combination of various disciplines
such as Genetics, Physiology, Ecology, Developmental Biology,
Microbiology, Parasitology, Entomology, Evolution, Taxonomy, Freshwater
Biology, Fisheries and Wildlife etc. This subject has significant role
in human resource development, food security, environmental
conservation, sustainable development and ultimately in alleviation of
poverty. Recently MS Programs both in Botany and Zoology were offered in Fall 2021. The Department of Biological Science

Vision & Mission
Our Vision
The inception of the Department of Zoology, driven by a vision to facilitate advanced studies and research in Zoology. Our curriculum is strategically engineered to harmonize with global scientific trends and industry demands. By bridging the gap between academic theory and real-world application, we transform students into high-caliber professionals, ready to excel in the world’s most competitive industrial and academic sectors. Your journey toward global impact begins here. Our Mission
The Department of Zoology is dedicated to fostering a dynamic academic environment that empowers individuals through intellectual curiosity and critical thinking. We achieve this by providing hands-on experience with cutting-edge computational tools, modern laboratory techniques, and advanced fieldwork methodologies. Nurturing creative, tolerant, and compassionate graduates who balance scientific expertise with a deep sense of social responsibility. Conducting high-impact research to address national challenges and contribute to the global body of zoological knowledge. Preparing highly skilled professionals capable of enriching public life and fueling innovation within academia, industry, and the economy of Pakistan. Core Values

Facilities & Laboratories
Zoology Laboratory
The department has a Research Labs of containing Colorimeter, Spectrophotometer and latest microscopic photographic system. In addition to the instrument Labs, the department has a Zoology Museum which have huge collection of vertebrates and invertebrates. Since the establishment of the department, a considerable addition of insects has been made from various areas of Gilgit-Baltistan. The research in the filed of insect taxonomy and pathology (freshwater and marine), protozoans, helminths, insects and other arthropods is undertaken by trained and experienced staff faculty of Science and Zoology. Help On Usage
Searching
There are 2 methods available on searching library catalog. The first one is SIMPLE SEARCH , which is the simplest method on searching catalog. You just enter any keyword, either it containes in titles, author(s) names or subjects. You can supply more than one keywords in Simple Search method and it will expanding your search results.
ADVANCED SEARCH , lets you define keywords in more specific fields. If you want your keywords only contained in title field, then type your keyword in Title field and the system will limit its search within Title fields only, not in other fields. Location field lets you narrowing search results by specific location, so only collection that exists in selected location get fetched by system.

title: Grading Policy
content:
Letter grading should only be used for representing the individual courses and not to report the semester GPA/CGPA.
a) The percentage of marks or values of grades other than grade points shall not be reported on the transcripts.
b) The minimum pass marks for each course as well as lab work shall be (fifty percent) 50%. A student obtaining less than 50% marks in any course/test shall be considered failed in that course/test. Less than 50% marks in any course shall not be counted towards the aggregate marks. The percentage of marks or values of grades other than grade points shall not be reported on the transcripts.
c) The minimum passing marks for each course as well as lab work shall be 50% (fifty percent). A student obtaining less than 50% marks in any course/test shall be considered failed in that course/test. Less than 50% marks in any course shall not be counted towards the aggregate marks.
d) The equivalence between letter grading and numerical grading shall be as follow: Percentage of marks shall be calculated up to one significant figure. If the first fraction after decimal is 4 or less, it shall be ignored. However, if the first fraction is 5 or more, it shall be taken into account by raising the percentage to the next higher digit.
e) The result of a student in each course having passed or failed shall be indicated on the transcript by letter grade. For a student completing his/her study program in the normal prescribed period / semesters, a mention to this effect shall be made in their transcripts.
f) Keeping in view the variations related to both academic systems (semester and annual system), the following equivalence of GPA/CGPA and percentage shall be the grading policy:
g) The grade points (G.P) policy shall be followed as per annexure A.

title: Definitions
content:
· Academic Program: Any combination of courses and/or requirements leading to award the university degrees/certificates, after the successful completion of all the prescribed requirements.
· Admission: Admission of a student as a regular student of the University of Baltistan, Skardu or in its constituent/affiliated college/institute/Sub-Campus(s).
· Dual Admission: Simultaneous admissions in more than one program of studies. Such cases shall be dealt as per HEC Policy in vogue.
· Admission Committee: A departmental committee notified for the purpose of admissions of the students who qualify the prescribed eligibility criteria for admission in a particular program.
· Affiliated Colleges: Those colleges which are affiliated with UoBS.
· Assessment: The assessment of the performance or achievement of the students in an academic program. This can include assessment tools such as assignments, examinations, practical (Lab) work/field work, project work, seminar papers, and tutorial participation etc. as per HEC relevant policy (as amended from time to time).
· Assignment: A task relevant to a course of study assigned to the student by concerned faculty member to substantiate the course contents. The assignment may or may not be graded.
· Associate Degree Program: A four-semester (two-year) undergraduate regular study program (offered as per HEC Policy in vogue).
· Cease: A student is considered unsuitable for further studies at The University of Baltistan, Skardu as a regular student for a specified time on disciplinary grounds by university authorities, as defined in The University of Baltistan Discipline Rules.
· Chairperson/ Head: Chairperson/Head of an academic department.
· Contact Hour: One contact hour means 60 minutes of teacher – student interaction (with 05 minutes break inclusive) spent on academic/research related activities including instructional work/tutorials, research work, projects, seminars, workshops etc. during the course of studies at the university.
· Controller: The Controller of Examinations of the University of Baltistan, Skardu.
· Course: A set of contents related to an academic Program, which is to be studied by a student for a fixed number of hours during a semester. Each subject will carry a specific discipline code and number.
· Credit Course: A “Credit Course” means a course of study, which shall be required for successful completion of the degree.
· Credit Hour (Cr. Hr): Credit hour in class means teaching/learning a theory course for one hour each week throughout the semester. One credit hour in laboratory or practical work/project would require lab contact of three hours per week.
· Cumulative Grade Point Average (CGPA): The summation of grade points of all credit courses divided by the total number of credit hours taken by a student.
· Dean: The Dean of a faculty in the University.
· Department: An Academic Department of the University of Baltistan, Skardu.
· Departmental Council : A committee including concerned Head of the Department and three senior faculty members of the department.
· Drop out: A student considered unsuitable upon academic performance for further studies at The University of Baltistan, Skardu or its Constituent Institute/ Affiliated College/Sub-campus and is removed from the roll of the University.
· Examinations: The semester examination.
· Examiner: A person appointed to conduct the examination.
· Faculty: A faculty of the University of Baltistan, Skardu.
· Grade: A mark (letter grade or number) indicating the assessment of student’s academic performance.2.25. Grade Point (GP): Number of grade points representing the letter grades scored by a student in a course.
· Grade Points of a Credit Course : Total number of points scored by a student in a credit course.

title: Definitions
content:
The semester examination. · Examiner: A person appointed to conduct the examination. · Faculty: A faculty of the University of Baltistan, Skardu. · Grade: A mark (letter grade or number) indicating the assessment of student’s academic performance.2.25. Grade Point (GP): Number of grade points representing the letter grades scored by a student in a course. · Grade Points of a Credit Course : Total number of points scored by a student in a credit course.
This number is the product of points representing the letter grade scored by the student in a course and the number of credit hours taken of the course.
· Grade Point Average (GPA): The average of the accumulative grade point earned in a semester or in the whole course of study.
· Internship: Students' engagement in a relevant academic, research or business organization related to the discipline chosen for specialization of maximum of three (03) Credit Hours offered in any upper division semester as per requirement of discipline.
· Make-up Exam: A Terminal exam for the students who could not appear for any genuine reason beyond human control or due to attending sports/national/international event on behalf of the University.
· Non-Credit Course: A course of study, which is required for the successful completion of the certificate/degree but the grade points are not going to be reflected in the CGPA.
· Practical/Laboratory (Lab) Test: These tests include all examinations/assessments to ascertain the level of competence of practical application of knowledge acquired.
· Project: A Project is an academic work aimed at determining the ability of a student to translate the theoretical knowledge acquired during a course of study into its practical application at Undergraduate Level.
· Probation: A student who does not excel academically and does not meet the requirements of the degree, said to be on probation if he/she is deficient in standards to the extent where he/she is likely to be relegated/withdrawn, is allowed to continue studies for one semester (in Two Years degree Program) and for two semesters (in Four Years degree Program).
· Research/Project Report: A report comprising the original research of a student/researcher which is counted towards the partial fulfillment of his/her degree subject to fulfillment of relevant prescribed procedure.
· Registrar: The Registrar of the University of Baltistan.
· Registration: Registration of the student in a teaching Department of the University.
· Research/Project Supervisor: A Teacher who supervises/guides Research/Project of an undergraduate/post graduate student till the successful completion of research work. The Supervisor shall have prescribed experience and relevant qualification in the field of research.
· Semester: A “Semester” is an academic period (mentioned in the Academic Calendar of the University), in which one set of courses in any discipline is offered.
· Teacher: A person serving in an academic department as lecturer, Assistant Professor, Associate Professor or Professor.
· Theory: A theory course is of 03 to 04 credit hours as per requirement of the discipline; time duration of the credit hour in class and lab.
· Undergraduate Program: A 16 years educational program including BS (4 Years), B.Sc. (Honors), MA/MSc. (2 Years) or equivalent Program.
· Unfair Means Review Committee: A committee appointed to deal with cases pertaining to use of unfair means in the examination by the students.
· UoBS : University of Baltistan, Skardu
· Vice Chancellor: The Vice Chancellor of the University of Baltistan, Skardu.

title: Admissions
content:
The University shall invite applications for admission in the various academic programs on prescribed application form through an advertisement by the student affairs via Registrar Office.
Eligibility Criteria for Various Programs
Each degree program shall have eligibility criteria for admissions set by Departmental Council according to HEC rules and conveyed to Admission Office.
Admission Procedure
a) Admissions for BS/Bachelor (4 years) degree programs shall be made once a year.
b) Admissions to BS/Bachelor (4 years) shall be announced preferably after the declaration of the results of HSSC examinations and the whole process shall be completed preferably 05 (Five) working days prior to commencement of the semester.
c) Admissions shall be open to all eligible candidates meeting the following criteria;
d) From Gilgit-Baltistan 80% of total seats in each discipline in each department.
e) From across Pakistan (excluding Gilgit-Baltistan) 20% of total seats in all programs of each department.
f) Foreign students seeking admissions in the University shall submit their applications through the HEC, Government of Pakistan. Such students shall be included in the 20% as described above.
g) Number of seats shall be defined by the respective Departmental Councils.
h) Admissions shall be open to all eligible candidates without discrimination on the basis of caste, creed, and gender.
i) The University shall invite applications for admissions to various academic programs on the prescribed application form, through an advertisement by the Admission Office indicating clearly number of open-merit seats as well as those on quota basis. The number of seats in each degree program shall be decided by the departmental council and conveyed to the Admission Office.
j) Advertisement for the admissions shall be published in at least one local and one national level certified daily newspapers as well as on the University Website. A period of minimum three (03) weeks shall be given for the application form submission.
k) Candidates shall apply online and submit the printed application form along with the following documents duly attested by an officer of BPS-17 or above.
l) Attested copies of S.S.C, H.S.S.C or equivalent examination certificates.
m) For the admissions in the graduate programs, attested copies of all earlier qualifications shall be submitted.
n) Attested copies of detail transcript.
o) Attested copy of character certificate from the head of the institution last attended.
p) Attested copy of domicile certificate.
q) Eight passport size photographs.
r) Migration certificate (original) within 30 days after admission.
s) Attested copy of computerized national identity card or form ‘B’.
t) Every application shall be accompanied by an affidavit (Annex-B) signed by the applicant and countersigned by his/her father/guardian stating that s/he shall abide by the Statutes, Rules and Regulations of the University.
u) Candidates applying for admissions to more than one programs and category (quota) shall submit separate application form and fee along with all supporting documents for each program and category (quota).

aa) All the candidates shall bring the relevant original documents for the inspection by the Departmental Admission Committee.

dd) Candidate selected for admission shall finalize the admission requirements within the notified period, failing which their right of admission shall be forfeited and the admission shall be offered to the next candidate on waiting list.
ee) Late admission shall be allowed to only those candidates who are on waiting list. Such candidates shall be informed about their selection by placing information on the University notice board, website and shall be required to finalize the admission requirements within the notified period.
ff) All candidates selected for admission shall be required to submit an undertaking at time of documents verification, on a judicial Stamp Paper of Rs. 30.

hh) All admissions shall remain provisional till verification of all the documents of newly admitted students by the Admission Office/ Student Affairs and Alumni. If a student is found guilty for submission of fake documents, his admission shall be cancelled immediately without any notice at any stage. The University reserves the right to pursue further legal formalities (if deemed necessary).
ii) Admission in one department shall not give any student a right of transfer to other department/migration to another university.
jj) The University may suspend any particular discipline if the number of applicants is less than 10 or due to any other reason. In such cases, the applicants may be considered for admission to another discipline subject to meeting prescribed eligibility criteria, merit and availability of seats.
kk) The following categories of candidates shall not be eligible for admissions:
· Who have got a degree/certificate with ‘third division’ in annual system or ’less than 50% marks or equivalent for other than annual system’ in the required qualification for admission to the specific program.
· Who have ceased to be students of this University/ any other university on disciplinary grounds.
· Who is already registered in any degree program in any institute. In case of dual registration, admission of the student shall be cancelled without any prior notice. HEC guidelines shall be followed in case of dual degrees.
ll) If a student fails to join a program during the first two weeks of the commencement of the semester as per announced schedule, his/her admission shall stand cancelled automatically without any prior notice.
mm) No change of discipline shall be entertained once the admissions are finalized.

title: Enrollment/Registration In Courses
content:
· All the Departments of the University shall have an advisor/Course Coordinator for each program on admission. The advisor and the student together shall develop a flexible comprehensive plan of study that shall be implemented in each semester. The advising file shall be updated each semester and shall include copies of transcripts and GPA earned.
· Students shall choose the courses they wish to enroll in, prior to the start of a semester with the advice of an advisor/course coordinator. For this purpose, the university shall publish a schedule for enrollment of students. Students shall make any change (add/drop) in the courses they are taking within second week of the semester and record the changes in Advisor/course coordinator file and office of the student Affairs.
· No drop and course registration shall be allowed after the third week of the semester.
· A student who wishes to add or drop a course, or change a section of a course after registration shall complete the relevant procedure as prescribed by the university.
· Students shall be allowed to withdraw from a course within 4-6 week of the semester.
· A student withdrawing after the 6th week shall be automatically awarded "F" grade which shall count in the GPA and stay on the transcript.
· HEC policy regarding dual degrees shall be followed by the University.

title: Message of the Vice-Chancellor
content:
Prof. Dr. Masood Akthar
Semester rules and regulations play a pivotal role in the smooth running of programmatic and programmatic activities in a university. I am delighted that our team has developed comprehensive rules and procedures for the use across the board. These rules and regulations are well-nested in the guidelines provided by the Higher Education Commission (HEC) and have been endorsed by the statutory bodies including the Academic Council and the Syndicate in their 3 rd and 7th meetings respectively. They reflect the vision, mission, and core values of the University of Baltistan, Skardu. Amendments to the rules will be made on a need basis and the changes will come in force after their endorsement by the relevant statutory bodies.
University of Baltistan, Skardu is a neophyte university aiming to provide quality higher education services to the immediate communities and elsewhere. The university, therefore, needs policies, rules, and procedures to be set from the very beginning. Alhamdullillah ! Our team is working hard in the formulation of policies and procedures with great enthusiasm and dedication!

title: Semester Rules Committee
content:
Realizing the importance of policies, procedures, and rules in order to run a novice university, Professor Dr. Muhammad Naeem Khan, the Vice Chancellor of the University of Baltistan, Skardu, had constituted a committee to develop semester rules for the university. Structure of the committee is as follows.
Dr. Ghulam Raza (Convener)
Mr. Waseem Ullah Jan Malik (Member)
Mr. Sajjad Hussain (Member)
Dr. Haji Karim Khan (Member)
Mr. Nasim Abbass (Co-Opted Member)
The committee worked on the rules religiously and presented the first draft in a faculty forum held in the Anchan Campus. The feedback received from the faculty and staff was incorporated in the draft and presented in the Third Academic Council held on December 11, 2019. On the recommendation of worthy Academic Council, for the review and feedback the draft was submitted to the Quality Enhancement Cell (QEC) .It was also suggested that the QEC reviewed document should be treated as the final (Recommendation of the Academic Council is attached as annexure E). The Chair of the committee submitted the document to the QEC on May 13, 2020. The QEC reviewed (the then Director QEC) the document thoroughly and shared its report on June 18, 2020 (The QEC report is attached as annexure F). As a result, the feedback/suggestions from the QEC have been incorporated in the current document. Upon the incorporation of all the feedback, the rules were once again presented in the 5th Academic Council meeting. The worthy Academic Council has approved the rules for the implementation.
These rules encompass all the details pertaining to the smooth running of semesters and programs. However, if required the rules shall be revised on the permission of the competent authority.
The Chair and members of the committee are grateful to the worthy Vice Chancellor, the worthy Academic Council and the senior management of UoBS for their trust and confidence in the committee. The Chair and members are also thankful to the then Director QEC (Dr. Haji Karim Khan) for the detailed and constructive feedback.
We appreciate the extraordinary work carried out by the current Controller of Examinations and his team members for religiously incorporating all the feedbacks and preparing the draft for the final printing. The Committee acknowledges the profound proofread carried out by Mr. Safeer Hussain, Head, Department of Languages & Cultural Studies and Deputy Director QEC of the University of Baltistan, Skardu.

title: Marking/Rechecking Of Examination Script
content:
The answer book of a candidate shall not be re-assessed under any circumstances whereas the re-checking does not mean re-assessment/re-evaluation/re-marking of the answer book. The Controller of Examination can arrange for re-checking of examination script by any faculty member from the relevant discipline on the complaint/request of students. The Controller of Examination or any officer or re-checking committee appointed shall see that:
a) There is no computational mistake in the grand total on the title page of the answer book.
b) The total of various parts of a question has been correctly made at the end of each question.
c) All totals have been correctly brought forward on the title page of the answer book.
d) No portion of any answer has been left un-marked.
e) Total marks in the answer book tally with the marks sheet.
f) The hand-writing of the candidate tally in the questions/answer book.
g) The candidate or anybody on his/her behalf has no right to see or examine the answer books for any purpose.
h) The marks of a candidate could even decrease in light of (c) above. In the event of reduction of marks the record shall be corrected accordingly and revised transcript shall be issued.

title: Course File
content:
Maintaining the Course File is compulsory for all faculty members. It shall have complete record of every activity that happens during the course. The course file should contain:
a) Course Code and Title.
b) Academic Calendar
c) Description of Course/Learning Outcomes.
d) Course Syllabus
e) Dates of Mid-Semester Examination.
f) Grading Policy shall identify each activity such as assignments, Quizzes, Mid- Semester Examination,Final Examination and Term Papers etc.
g) Copy of each Homework Assignment, Copy of each Quiz Assigned.
h) Copy of Question Papers for Mid Semester Examination.
i) Copy of Question Papers for Final/Semester End Examination.
j) Grading Sheets of the Course, Detailing Statistical Data on the Grades obtained by Students.
k) Difficulties/Problems faced by the Teacher and Students during Classroom/ Course Delivery.

title: Awards And Distinctions
content:
a) Medals/Prizes/Rolls of Honor/Positions shall be awarded to the students passing their internal as well as external examinations/term papers in the Annual as well as Semester System in the first attempt.
b) In the Semester System, Letter Grades shall be awarded on the basis of GP / GPA / CGPA and Positions would be given on the basis of CGPA. In case two or more students acquire same CGPA the Position shall be decided on the basis of percentage among those students.
c) The disciplines where number of students is less than 05, no position shall be awarded in semester system.
d) No medal and roll of honor shall be granted to candidates who passed the examination in 2nd attempt.
e) If the result of the candidate is not declared within the prescribed time of the degree, then no medal shall be awarded.
f) No Medal/Roll of Honor shall be awarded in the case of improving CGPA.

title: Semesters
content:
a) There shall be two regular semesters (Fall, Spring) in an academic year. Fall/Spring semesters shall spread over 16-18 weeks (inclusive of 1 – 2 weeks for exams).
b) UoBS is at liberty to enroll students (if they fulfill their admission criteria) for Fall/Spring semester or for any single course and issue transcript with letter grades at the end of the semester, depending on the availability of staff and necessary facilities.
c) Foreign students under student exchange program shall be enrolled for any semester or for any single course and UoBS shall issue transcript with letter grades at the end of the semester. Admission offer letter of the foreign student shall be forwarded to the HEC for issuance of NOC.

title: Grace Mark
content:
A student may submit an appeal regarding a grievance in relation to a grade to the Chairperson of the concerned Department within seven (07) calendar days of the declaration of the result. The Chairperson of the Department shall refer the appeal to the Departmental Examination Committee for consideration and recommendation. The Departmental Examination Committee shall examine the grievance and submit its recommendation to the Chairperson of the Department. The decision of the Chairperson shall be final, subject to the provisions regarding grace marks specified below. On the recommendation of the Departmental Examination Committee, the Chairperson may approve up to five (05) grace marks where a student is unable to progress/complete the relevant academic requirement due to a deficiency of marks in one paper or in the prescribed aggregate, subject to the applicable University rules. At the completion of the degree requirements, the Dean of the Faculty, on the recommendation of the Chairperson of the Department and the Departmental Examination Committee, may, as a one-time concession during the entire degree program, approve up to five (05) grace marks for a student who is deficient by not more than five (05) marks from the immediately higher grade. A student shall not be entitled to receive more than five (05) grace marks in total under these provisions during the entire degree program.

The Chairperson of the Department shall refer the appeal to the Departmental Examination Committee for consideration and recommendation.

At the completion of the degree requirements, the Dean of the Faculty, on the recommendation of the Chairperson of the Department and the Departmental Examination Committee, may, as a one-time concession during the entire degree program, approve up to five (05) grace marks for a student who is deficient by not more than five (05) marks from the immediately higher grade.
A student shall not be entitled to receive more than five (05) grace marks in total under these provisions during the entire degree program.

title: Course Load
content:
Undergraduate Programs
a) An undergraduate program of instruction generally includes a 15-18 Credit Hours course load including exams in a regular semester. The required course load for a fulltime undergraduate is 15 credit hours per semester (minimum).
b) In case any student wishes to enroll for one more course beyond 18 Cr. Hours, s/he shall be allowed by institution in either of the given cases:
· If his/her CGPA is above 3.5 and
· The student needs the course to graduate on time and
· In case of repeating /failed/dropped courses with the prior permission of the Chairperson/Head of the Department/Principal concerned.
Graduate Programs
a) A graduate student shall enroll for 9-12 credit hours in a regular semester. He/she shall take at least nine (09) credit hours in Fall and Spring semesters to be considered as a full-time student.
b) The University shall allow a student to take additional courses (maximum 04 credit hours) in a semester depending on circumstances with the advice of the advisor, HoD and course coordinator.

title: Freezing Of Semester
content:
a) A student shall be allowed to freeze two semester(s) at a time or separately before the commencement of Mid-term examination. Applications received after this deadline shall not be entertained.
b) The student shall resume the frozen/same semester whenever offered by the University/Institute,
c) No freezing in the first semester shall be allowed.
d) Freezing up to two semesters (combined or separately) shall be allowed to students facing acute domestic problems/valid reasons subject to approval of Vice Chancellor on the recommendation of the Chairperson/HOD/Principal concerned.
e) For frozen semester the student shall pay 25% of tuition fee for each semester to continue his/her registration with the University of Baltistan, Skardu.
f) The process of freezing of semester and restoration/de-freezing shall be done by the Academic Section of Registrar Office.
g) In special hardship cases, the University shall develop criteria for freezing a semester with the prior permission of the Vice Chancellor. Medical certificate shall be duly signed by the University Medical Officer.
h) Freezing of first two semesters for BS and first semester for MS is not allowed.
i) Under special hardship circumstances freezing of first semester can be considered upon the approval of competent authority under the following circumstances/conditions.
· Iddat
· Maternity/Delivery
· Death in the immediate family
· Any other subject to acceptance on justified rationale
Note: Freezing of Semester shall only be allowed after successful completion of 1st Semester as prerequisite as the case may be for other semester’s predecessor to the freezing Semester.
